skill.name: pathml
skill.description: Guide PathML workflows for whole-slide pathology images, preprocessing, spatial graphs, machine learning, multiparametric imaging, and HDF5 data management.
skill.summary: PathML guidance for computational pathology, WSI processing, spatial graphs, and pathology model workflows.
skill.author: davila7

security_audit.summary: Most static findings are false positives from Markdown documentation, inline code names, PyTorch eval mode, HDF5 examples, or local filesystem examples. Confirmed risk remains for the documented DeepCell remote API workflow and for a copied SLURM shell-script example with unquoted path handling. No evidence found of prompt injection, hidden exfiltration logic, or executable marketplace hooks.

remediation.issue: Remote DeepCell API examples could expose regulated pathology data.
remediation.suggestion: Add a privacy warning, require explicit consent, and recommend local SegmentMIF for sensitive or clinical datasets.

remediation.issue: The SLURM example passes slide paths through shell commands without clear quoting guidance.
remediation.suggestion: Quote "$SLIDE_PATH", validate slide list paths, and document safe job submission practices.

remediation.issue: Documentation includes setup and processing commands that users may copy directly.
remediation.suggestion: Label commands as examples and remind users to review environment, paths, permissions, and dependencies before running them.

content.value_statement: Whole-slide image workflows require careful handling of formats, tiles, models, and storage. This skill provides PathML guidance for loading, preprocessing, graph analysis, machine learning, and multiparametric imaging.
actual_capabilities: Explains WSI loading workflows for SVS, NDPI, DICOM, OME-TIFF, CODEX, Vectra, and related formats.
Guides preprocessing pipelines for stain normalization, tissue detection, nucleus detection, and artifact labeling.
Covers tile generation, pyramid level selection, HDF5 storage, and memory-efficient batch processing.
Describes spatial graph construction, feature extraction, neighborhood analysis, and graph export workflows.
Outlines model training, evaluation, ONNX export, and inference workflows for pathology models.
Supports multiparametric imaging guidance for marker quantification, segmentation, and AnnData integration.
limitations: Provides guidance and examples, but does not include executable PathML source code.
Requires users to supply local image files, annotations, models, and environment dependencies.
Clinical use needs validation, privacy review, and regulatory controls outside the skill.
Remote DeepCell examples may send data to third-party services and require consent.

use_cases.title: Build WSI Preprocessing Pipelines

use_cases.title: Analyze Multiplex Tissue Images
use_cases.description: Design CODEX or Vectra workflows for segmentation, marker quantification, and AnnData export.

use_cases.title: Prepare Model Training Workflows
use_cases.description: Organize datasets, loaders, metrics, and inference plans for pathology machine learning models.

prompt_templates.title: Plan Slide Loading
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the PathML skill to outline a WSI loading plan for [format], [number] slides, and [analysis goal]. Include pyramid level guidance.

prompt_templates.title: Design Preprocessing
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a PathML preprocessing plan for [stain or modality]. Include quality control, tile settings, transforms, and storage outputs.

prompt_templates.title: Build Spatial Analysis
prompt_templates.prompt: Design a cell graph workflow for [modality] with segmentation masks, marker features, neighborhood metrics, and visualization outputs.

prompt_templates.title: Architect Training Pipeline
prompt_templates.prompt: Plan a PathML machine learning workflow for [task]. Include dataset preparation, loaders, metrics, validation, inference, and deployment constraints.

output_examples.input: A researcher asks how to process 500 H&E slides for nucleus analysis.
output_examples.output: A staged plan covering slide inspection, tile generation, stain normalization, nucleus detection, HDF5 outputs, and batch processing controls.

output_examples.input: A spatial biology team asks how to analyze CODEX marker expression.
output_examples.output: A workflow for loading CODEX data, collapsing channels, segmenting cells, quantifying markers, exporting AnnData, and validating outputs.

output_examples.input: An engineer asks how to evaluate a HoVer-Net model on held-out slides.
output_examples.output: A checklist for dataset splits, loaders, inference mode, segmentation metrics, error review, and model export planning.

best_practices: Validate slide formats, magnification, metadata, and permissions before scaling batch processing.
Start with thumbnails and small tile subsets before processing complete slide cohorts.
Keep raw data separate from processed HDF5 outputs and document all processing parameters.
anti_patterns: Run remote segmentation on sensitive clinical images without privacy approval.
Load full-resolution slides into memory before checking pyramid levels and tile sizes.
Use model outputs for clinical decisions without validation, review, and governance.

faq.question: What is this skill for?
faq.answer: It helps plan and explain PathML workflows for digital pathology image analysis and machine learning.

faq.question: Does the skill process image files by itself?
faq.answer: No. It provides guidance and examples for tools that users run in their own environment.

faq.question: Which image formats are covered?
faq.answer: It covers common WSI and multiplex formats such as SVS, NDPI, DICOM, OME-TIFF, CODEX, and Vectra.

faq.question: Can it help with spatial proteomics?
faq.answer: Yes. It covers CODEX and multiplex workflows, marker quantification, segmentation, and AnnData integration.

faq.question: Is it suitable for clinical diagnosis?
faq.answer: No. Clinical use requires independent validation, privacy controls, regulatory review, and qualified professional oversight.

faq.question: Does it use remote services?
faq.answer: Some examples describe remote DeepCell segmentation. Users should prefer local processing for sensitive or regulated data.
